newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Spanish league championship
matches this weekend:
Playing Saturday:
Rayo Vallecano (18) v Valencia (9) (Kickff 1815GMT)
Desperate Rayo could play several reserve team players,
while club captain Ramon de Quintana has called upon Rayo fans
for special support against a Valencia side that is still
bidding for a UEFA Cup place.
Real Betis (4) v Sporting Gijon (17) (2030)
Betis have agreed to play the game on Saturday night to
compensate for the refusal to allow television cameras into a
game earlier in the season. Defender Avelino Riopedre returns
from a three-month lay-off for Sporting.
Playing Sunday:
Celta Vigo (14) v Athletic Bilbao (6) (1600)
An avalanche of injuries have hit a Celta side who have
drifted into relegation trouble, while Athletic are still
revelling from last Sunday's victory over Real Madrid. The
fixture has ended in three consecutive draws.
Real Sociedad (8) v Tenerife (10) (1600)
Real striker Gheorghe Craioveanu is likely to miss the rest
of the season with a muscle strain, while club chairman Luis
Uranga is banned from the VIP box for insulting a referee. Both
sides need a result to maintain their UEFA Cup aspirations.
Espanyol (15) v Logrones (22) (1600)
Logrones are already relegated and looking for a new manager
for next season, while Espanyol need a win to avoid last-minute
relegation worries and will be without suspended defender
Mauricio Pochettino..
Deportivo Coruna (3) v Valladolid (7) (1600)
Deportivo no longer have anything to play for, but could
decide the UEFA Cup hopes of Valladolid, who look set to bring
back Croatian sharpshooter Alen Peternac.
Racing Santander (13) v Compostela (12) (1700)
Compostela defender Francisco Villena is doubtful for a game
between two sides that despite their league positions could yet
be hit by last-minute relegation worries.
Oviedo (16) v Sevilla (20) (1700)
Sevilla could end the day relegated to the second division,
and must repeat their victories in two of the past three seasons
at fellow strugglers Oviedo, who will be without Abel Xavier for
the rest of the season because of a leg injury.
Real Madrid (1) v Extremadura (19) (1700)
Real welcome back strikers Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic
from suspension but will be without set-piece ace Roberto
Carlos, who is with the Brazilian national side, while
Extremadura will be supported by over 1,000 fans, around five
percent of the population of their home town, Almendraljeo.
Hercules (21) v Barcelona (2) (1730)
Barcelona were boosted last weekend by being let back into
the title chase by Real Madrid, but have been rocked during the
week by the announcement that Ronaldo will leave the club.
Hercules will be relegated unless they win.
Playing Monday:
Zaragoza (11) v Atletico Madrid (5) (1930)
A game between two sides with nothing to play for, as
Zaragoza are out of relegation trouble but have no realistic
European hopes, while Atletico have already guaranteed a UEFA
Cup place.
